tell_vi: "Điều này có nghĩa là" mở đầu câu giải thích
tell_en: A which-means-that clause translated word for word
why_it_happens: English chains explanation with a relative clause; Vietnamese chains it with a full stop and a new subject
fix: Cut the connector. State the consequence as its own sentence: "Bạn không phải chờ." A Vietnamese reader gets the causal link from order alone

tell_vi: Bị động có tác nhân: "được nấu bởi đầu bếp"
tell_en: Agentive passive with bởi, copied from English by-phrases
why_it_happens: English marks the agent inside the passive; Vietnamese normally fronts the agent and drops the passive entirely
fix: Front the agent: "Đầu bếp nấu nồi này từ 4 giờ sáng." Keep được only where the agent genuinely does not matter

tell_vi: Danh từ hoá thừa: "sự tối ưu hoá", "việc triển khai"
tell_en: Nominalised verbs stacked to mimic English noun phrases
detect_regex: (?i)\b(sự|việc) (tối ưu|triển khai|cải thiện|nâng cao|đảm bảo|tăng cường|phát triển|tìm|lựa chọn|phục vụ|sử dụng|mua|thanh toán|giao hàng|chăm sóc|trải nghiệm|kết nối)
why_it_happens: English abstract nouns have no natural Vietnamese equivalent, so sự/việc gets bolted on
fix: Return the verb to the sentence: "Chúng tôi cắt sáu ca không cần thiết" thay cho "việc tối ưu hoá nhân sự"

tell_vi: "Một trong những … nhất"
tell_en: One-of-the-most, transliterated
why_it_happens: It is the standard rendering of a standard English brag, and it survives translation because it is grammatical
fix: Replace with the number or drop the claim: "Quán thứ ba ở phố này" is checkable; "một trong những quán ngon nhất" is not

tell_vi: "Trong thế giới ngày nay", "Trong thời đại số"
tell_en: In-today's-world opener
why_it_happens: The most common LLM essay opener in English, translated intact
fix: Delete the sentence. Open on the reader's own next forty minutes, not on the century

tell_vi: "Hãy tưởng tượng…" mở bài
tell_en: Imagine-that opener
why_it_happens: Imported hook formula; Vietnamese ads more often state the situation as fact
fix: State it: "Trưa nay bạn có bốn mươi phút." The reader does not need to be asked to imagine their own life

tell_vi: "Hãy" trước mọi động từ
tell_en: Hãy prefixed to every imperative, copying English let's/please
why_it_happens: English softens commands with let's and please; Vietnamese imperatives are already polite in context
fix: Keep at most one hãy per piece, on the actual CTA. "Ghé trước 11h30" is a complete instruction

tell_vi: "Không chỉ … mà còn …"
tell_en: Not-only-but-also, the highest-frequency empty contrast
why_it_happens: It manufactures contrast without requiring a fact, in both languages
fix: Name the two facts as two sentences, or admit there is only one fact and cut the construction

tell_vi: Chuỗi "Hơn nữa / Ngoài ra / Bên cạnh đó / Cuối cùng"
tell_en: Furthermore-additionally-moreover ladder, translated
detect_regex: (?i)(^|[.!?…]\s+)(hơn nữa|ngoài ra|bên cạnh đó|thêm vào đó|cuối cùng nhưng không kém quan trọng)
why_it_happens: Essay scaffolding leaks from the English draft into the Vietnamese one
fix: Delete them all. If two paragraphs need a word to connect them, the second paragraph is in the wrong place

tell_vi: "Uy tín, chuyên nghiệp, tận tâm, chất lượng đảm bảo"
tell_en: The trust-adjective stack every Vietnamese business page carries
detect_regex: (?i)(uy tín|chuyên nghiệp|tận tâm|chất lượng (cao|đảm bảo)|giá cả hợp lý|đa dạng mẫu mã)
why_it_happens: They are free to write, nobody has ever been sued over them, and every competitor uses them, so they read as wallpaper
fix: One verifiable thing each: years at one address, the licence number, the return window, the actual price

tell_vi: "Chúng tôi tự hào là…"
tell_en: We-are-proud-to-be opener
why_it_happens: Self-congratulation is the default company voice in both languages
fix: Move the sentence to the reader's side: what they get, stated as a fact they can check

tell_vi: Gạch ngang em dash trong tiếng Việt
tell_en: Em dashes used mid-sentence in Vietnamese prose
why_it_happens: Vietnamese punctuation uses commas, colons and full stops for this job; the em dash arrives with the English draft
fix: Replace with a comma, a colon or a full stop. Keep the en dash only for ranges and dialogue

tell_vi: Tiêu Đề Viết Hoa Từng Chữ
tell_en: Title Case applied to a Vietnamese heading
why_it_happens: English headline capitalisation copied onto Vietnamese, where only the first word and proper nouns take capitals
fix: Sentence case: "Bốn món, không món nào là món phụ"

tell_vi: "Let's…" dịch từ "Hãy…"
tell_en: Let's opening a sentence aimed at a customer, carried over from hãy
why_it_happens: Vietnamese hãy is neutral; English let's is first-person-plural and puts the brand inside the reader's decision
fix: Second person imperative: "Come before 11:30." Or state the fact and let the reader act

tell_vi: "Prestigious" dịch từ "uy tín"
tell_en: Prestigious, reputable, dedicated, wholeheartedly — the uy tín family in English
why_it_happens: Dictionary equivalents of Vietnamese trust words that read as unearned puffery in English
fix: Substitute the evidence the Vietnamese word was standing in for: the years, the address, the guarantee

tell_vi: "Reasonable price" dịch từ "giá cả hợp lý"
tell_en: Reasonable price, affordable price, diverse products
why_it_happens: Direct rendering of standard Vietnamese retail copy; in English it signals cheap without saying a number
fix: Print the number, or the comparison the number supports

tell_vi: "Wish you…" dịch từ "Chúc bạn…"
tell_en: Wish-you closings and Thank-you-for-trusting-us sign-offs
detect_regex: (?i)\b(wish you|thank you for (trusting|believing in|choosing to trust))
why_it_happens: Vietnamese closings are formulaic and warm; the literal English reads like a form letter
fix: End on the next action, with a time on it. Warmth in English comes from specificity, not from blessing

tell_vi: "Tiêu chuẩn 5 sao", "đẳng cấp quốc tế"
tell_en: 5-star standard, international class, world-class, top-notch
why_it_happens: Vietnamese market shorthand for quality, meaningless in English unless a body actually awarded it
fix: Name the certifying body and the year, or delete

tell_vi: "Very" thay cho từ mạnh hơn
tell_en: Very, really, extremely doing the work a precise word should do
why_it_happens: Vietnamese rất is unmarked and frequent; the English equivalents are marked and weaken the sentence
fix: One stronger word, or a number. "Very fast" becomes "8 minutes"

tell_vi: "Please" trước mọi câu, dịch từ "vui lòng"
tell_en: Please prefixed to every instruction
why_it_happens: Vui lòng is neutral register in Vietnamese; repeated please in English reads as pleading
fix: Keep one please at the point of real imposition. Elsewhere use the plain imperative

tell_vi: Tiêu đề "About …" dịch từ "Về …"
tell_en: About-X headings where the section is actually a claim
why_it_happens: Về X is the default Vietnamese section label and translates to a heading that promises nothing
fix: Make the heading the claim: "Same pot, same corner, nine years"

tell_vi: Chuỗi "X, which is Y, which means Z" — hai mệnh đề quan hệ nối nhau
tell_en: The which-chain: two or more relative clauses hooked together in one sentence
why_it_happens: One long sentence is cheaper to generate than three short ones with a decision about order
fix: Split at the second which. Order the sentences so each earns the next. A single which-clause is fine; the chain is the tell

tell_vi: "Furthermore / Moreover / In conclusion"
tell_en: Essay connectives in marketing copy
detect_regex: (?i)\b(furthermore|moreover|additionally|in conclusion|that said|it(’|'|\s+i)s worth noting|ultimately|at the end of the day)\b
why_it_happens: Trained-in academic scaffolding; it summarises instead of pulling the reader forward
fix: Delete on sight. Replace with an unanswered question, a number handoff, or a concession-then-turn

tell_vi: Tính từ thay bằng chứng: premium, exceptional
tell_en: Adjectives standing in for evidence: premium, exceptional, seamless, cutting-edge, robust
why_it_happens: Adjectives are free and evidence is expensive
fix: One number, one named source, or one thing the reader can verify, per claim

tell_vi: Mở bài bằng câu hỏi tu từ
tell_en: Opening on a rhetorical question the reader never asked
why_it_happens: A question is the cheapest way to start when the writer has not decided what the first fact is
fix: Open on the fact. A question earns its place only when the next line answers it with a number

tell_vi: Cái gì cũng liệt kê ba ý
tell_en: Everything arrives in threes
why_it_happens: Three is the most satisfying rhetorical count, so it becomes every count
fix: Let some lists be two and some be five. Three is correct when there are exactly three things

tell_vi: "Một trong những … nhất" dịch sang tiếng Anh
tell_en: One of the most / leading / top, with nothing measuring it
why_it_happens: The direct English rendering of một trong những … nhất, which is the default Vietnamese brag and survives translation because it is grammatical
fix: Replace with the rank and the source, or the number underneath it. "Third on this street since 2009" is checkable

tell_vi: "kinh nghiệm trong nghề" dịch nguyên cụm
tell_en: Experience in the profession / in the field, translated whole
why_it_happens: trong nghề is idiomatic in Vietnamese and redundant in English, where the years alone carry it
fix: Cut the phrase. "A chef of twenty years" says it, and the number is the only part that was working

tell_vi: "ưu tiên hàng đầu" dịch nguyên cụm
tell_en: Always our top priority, our number one concern
why_it_happens: ưu tiên hàng đầu is standard Vietnamese business register; in English it is a promise with no mechanism attached
fix: Name what you actually do about it: the return window, the replacement rule, the hours somebody answers the phone

tell_vi: "Trong thế giới ngày nay" dịch sang tiếng Anh
tell_en: In today's world / in today's fast-paced digital age opener
why_it_happens: The single most common LLM essay opener in English, and the source of the Vietnamese calque trong thế giới ngày nay
fix: Delete the sentence. Open on the reader's own next forty minutes, not on the century

tell_vi: "Ngươi" dùng để gọi khách
tell_en: The obsolete second person `ngươi` used to address a customer
why_it_happens: Machine translation reaches for a dictionary `you` with no age and no rank attached, and `ngươi` is the only Vietnamese pronoun that looks like one; it reads as costume drama
fix: Decide who the reader is, then hold it: `bạn` for a peer, `anh`/`chị` for a stranger you respect, `quý khách` when the surface is ceremonial. See references/address-register.md

tell_vi: "Người ta nói/cho rằng" thay cho một nguồn
tell_en: `Người ta` plus a verb of saying, standing in for evidence
why_it_happens: It is the widest-reference pronoun in Vietnamese - they, people, one, someone - so it is where `studies show` and `experts agree` land when there is no study and no expert
fix: Name the source or drop the claim. If it is your own data say so and give the number and the date

tell_vi: "Kính thưa quý vị" mở đầu một bài đăng
tell_en: A ceremonial vocative opening ordinary commercial copy
why_it_happens: It is the register of a wedding MC and a conference stage, and it arrives whenever the English draft said `Dear valued customer` or the writer wanted to sound respectful by default
fix: Open on the reader's own situation. Keep `quý khách` for the surfaces that earn it - a formal quote, a press release - and never on social

tell_vi: "Kính gửi quý khách hàng thân mến" dịch sang tiếng Anh
tell_en: Dear valued customer / esteemed client
why_it_happens: A form letter's way of addressing someone whose name it does not have; in Vietnamese it comes back as `kính gửi quý khách hàng` and freezes the whole piece at ceremonial tier
fix: Use the name if you have it. If you do not, open on what the reader ordered or asked about

tell_vi: "Quý vị khách quý" trong bản tiếng Anh
tell_en: Honoured / esteemed / distinguished guests, customers, clients
why_it_happens: Flattery used as a substitute for a reason to keep reading, and the direct source of the Vietnamese `quý vị` opener on channels where nobody speaks that way
fix: Cut the address entirely and start with the offer, the date or the number
